insight.insight: Probes fail out of distribution because of where they place their weight, not because the information is missing. The 100-PC source basis holds enough signal to separate deceptive from honest responses on every target, but a source-trained probe leans on source-specific surface directions. A small subset of source PCs that encode the honest/deceptive contrast abstractly does transfer. That subset can be partly found without target data by having an LLM judge score natural-language interpretations of each PC.
dependent_results: Target-trained probes restricted to the top-100 source PCs reach 0.936 / 0.950 / 0.869 AUROC. Source-trained full-representation baselines reach only 0.706 (IT Report), 0.874 (IT Confirm) and 0.606 (Sandbagging). (4.1 Setting a baseline)

A target-guided greedy search over source PCs selects about 15 / 8 / 14 PCs. Source-trained probes on these PCs nearly match target-trained probes, improving on the baseline by 0.22 AUROC on IT Report and 0.23 on Sandbagging. Top-k-by-variance PCs match greedy only on IT Confirm. (4.2 Showing a transferable subspace exists)

Ranking PCs by source-probe standardized weights transfers about as well as the baseline. Ranking by target-probe weights does well on IT Report, is worse than greedy on IT Confirm, and is below chance on Sandbagging. Jaccard overlap between greedy and target-PCA sets is 0.182 / 0.077 / 0.167. (4.3 Testing hypotheses for transferable principal components; Appendix D)
Of the 5 PCs that greedy selected for more than one target, 3 received the maximum OOD score (6). Only 1 of the top 5 source-probe PCs did. (4.4 Interpreting the transferable subspace)

A probe on the 19 interp-selected PCs, using no target data, beats the baseline, the top-19-by-variance control and the 81-PC ablation on all targets. It closes 78% of the baseline-to-greedy gap on IT Report (0.706→0.881 vs 0.929) and 25% on Sandbagging (0.606→0.662 vs 0.832). (4.5 Selecting a subspace by interpreting PCs; 5 Limitations)
key_definitions: Source-domain PCA basis: source activations (layer-15, mean over assistant tokens) are standardized, and PCA keeps the top 100 PCs. Targets are standardized with source statistics. Probes on a subset S are trained on projections onto S. (3 Setup)
Probe: logistic regression with λ=10, evaluated by AUROC on held-out target datasets. Ambiguous labels are removed. (3 Setup)

Greedy oracle: PCs are added one at a time, each chosen to maximize target AUROC of a source-trained probe. It stops when the improvement is ≤0.001, uses 5-fold CV over the target, and serves as an upper bound rather than an unbiased OOD estimate. (4.2 Showing a transferable subspace exists)

Standardized coefficient: the absolute probe coefficient times the standard deviation of its PC. It is used to rank PCs for the source-PCA and target-PCA probes. (4.3 Testing hypotheses for transferable principal components)

OOD score: a GPT-5-mini rating from 1 to 10 of how useful a PC direction is for out-of-distribution deception detection. It is based on the 8 most and 8 least activating source examples. Interp-selected PCs are those scoring the observed maximum of 6 in both of two runs (19 PCs). (4.4 Interpreting the transferable subspace; Appendix B)
Gap closed: (interp AUROC − baseline) / (greedy AUROC − baseline). (4.5 Selecting a subspace by interpreting PCs)
reasoning_steps: The top-100 source PCs are chosen because lower-index PCs align better with SAE features and so are easier to interpret. This choice is not a claim that they generalize better. (3 Setup; Appendix C)
Target-trained probes do well within the 100-PC subspace, so the poor source transfer comes from the direction the source probe learns, not from missing information. (4.1 Setting a baseline)

Greedy target-guided selection finds a small subset that transfers. Variance-matched controls fail, so which PCs are chosen matters, and variance does not predict it. (4.2 Showing a transferable subspace exists)

Neither source-probe nor target-probe weight rankings recover the greedy subset. Transferable PCs are therefore neither the most source-discriminative nor the most target-discriminative. Source-heavy PCs appear to encode surface features. (4.3 Testing hypotheses for transferable principal components)

The LLM judge's interpretations give the maximum score to most PCs that greedy selected across multiple targets, but to few source-heavy PCs. This suggests transferable PCs encode the contrast more abstractly. (4.4 Interpreting the transferable subspace)

Training on the judge-selected PCs without target data, then comparing against variance and ablation controls, shows that interpretability-driven subspace selection partly recovers oracle transfer. This supports reframing OOD robustness as a subspace-selection problem. (4.5 Selecting a subspace by interpreting PCs; 6 Conclusion)
